1	# kolosok-rehack — AI Development Guidelines
2	
3	Team **Kolosok** at the **European Hackathon League (EHL) Grand Finale**, Munich (TUM.ai).
4	This file is the rulebook for every AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) and human working in this repo.
5	**Read it fully before your first change.** Human setup (GitHub token, credentials) lives in `README-Human`.
6	
7	Source: [EHL Finale – All you need to know](https://tum-ai.notion.site/REDACTED)
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 0. Hard rules (non-negotiable)
12	
13	1. **Entire must be enabled and every commit must carry a checkpoint.** The organisers will reject a submission that does not use Entire. No Entire → no valid submission.
14	2. **All work goes through git and gets pushed to `origin`.** Nothing that exists only on one laptop counts.
15	3. **`main` must always be demo-able.** We have a strict 6-minute slot for pitch + demo + questions.
16	4. **Never commit secrets** (API keys, tokens, `.env`). Entire redacts secrets in session logs, but do not rely on that.
17	5. **Never rewrite pushed history** (no `push --force`, no amending/rebasing pushed commits, no deleting `entire/*` branches or refs). Checkpoints are tied to commits; rewriting history can orphan them.
18	
19	## 1. Key times (Munich local time)
20	
21	| When | What |
22	|---|---|
23	| Sat 10 Oct, 11:00–11:30 | Entire technical onboarding |
24	| **Sat 10 Oct, 13:00** | **Challenge selection deadline** (captain, on https://ehl.gg/) |
25	| Sat 13:30 → Sun 12:00 | Hacking |
26	| **Sun 11 Oct, 12:00** | **Submission deadline** — hard stop |
27	| Sun 12:00–14:30 | Challenge pitches (6 min incl. Q&A) |
28	| Sun 15:30–16:30 | Main-stage final (6 teams) |
29	
30	Internal targets: **feature freeze Sun 10:00**, first full submission by **Sun 10:30**, final re-submission by **11:45**.
31	Submissions can be repeated as often as we like before the deadline, so submit early and update.
32	
33	**Challenge:** BMW Group — AI for Product Decision Making: an app that turns customer feedback, product/sales data and web research into prioritized, PM-reviewed customer requirements with a full audit trail. Details: [`BMW-Challenge.md`](BMW-Challenge.md).
34	
35	## 2. Setup checklist (each machine, once)
36	
37	Prerequisites: `git` on `PATH` (Entire shells out to it — it fails with `exec: "git": executable file not found` otherwise).
38	
39	```bash
40	# 1. Install Entire (bash / Git Bash). On Windows the binary ends up in ~/.local/bin/entire.exe
41	curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
42	
43	# 2. On the main branch of this repo:
44	git checkout main && git pull
45	git config pull.rebase true      # plain `git pull` makes merge commits, which carry no checkpoint
46	entire login                     # if not logged in yet
47	entire enable                    # enables session tracking in this repo
48	entire agent add claude-code     # install hooks for your agent; `entire agent list` shows others (codex, cursor, …)
49	
50	# 3. Verify
51	entire status
52	entire doctor                    # if anything looks off
53	```
54	
55	**You are set up correctly when** your next commit prints:
56	
57	```
58	[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done
59	```
60	
61	If you don't see that line, stop and fix Entire before writing more code.
62	
63	## 3. Git workflow
64	
65	- **Commit small and often** — at least every meaningful step, ideally every 15–30 min of agent work. Each commit becomes a checkpoint linking the code to the prompt/reasoning behind it.
66	- **Commit only from within a tracked agent session**, after the agent made the change with its file-edit tools. Hand-made commits, merge commits and shell (`sed`, `echo >`) edits get no checkpoint.
67	- **After every commit** check the checkpoint is there: `git log -1 --format=%B` must show an `Entire-Checkpoint:` line. If it is missing, fix it *before* pushing.
68	- **Commit messages:** imperative, prefixed by area, e.g. `feat(api): add route planner endpoint`, `fix(ui): handle empty results`, `docs: update run instructions`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `chore`, `test`, `demo`.
69	- **Sync before push:** `git pull --rebase` on *unpushed* local commits only, then `git push`. Resolve conflicts, never discard teammates' work.
70	- **Branches:** short-lived feature branches (`feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`) merged back to `main` quickly (within a few hours). Trivial fixes may go straight to `main`. Do not let branches drift overnight.
71	- **Do not commit:** `.env`, credentials, `node_modules/`, virtualenvs, large datasets or model weights, build artifacts. Add them to `.gitignore` as soon as they appear.
72	- **After every push** check the `[entire] Pushing … checkpoint ref(s)` line appeared.
73	
74	## 4. How agents should work here
75	
76	**Before starting a task**
77	1. Read this README, `README-Human` and **`VISION.md`** (our product idea, shared context for everyone); look at `Concept/` for the architecture sketch (`root.drawio`).
78	2. `git pull` and check what others (human or agent) are doing:
79	   - `entire recap` — summary of recent checkpoint activity
80	   - `entire session list` — active/past agent sessions
81	   - `entire checkpoint search "<topic>"` — has someone already tried this?
82	3. Confirm the task is not already in progress to avoid duplicate work.
83	
84	**While working**
85	- Keep scope tight: do the requested task, nothing more. Hackathon time is the scarcest resource.
86	- Prefer simple, working solutions over clever ones; a reliable demo beats extra features.
87	- Match existing structure, naming, and style. Don't introduce new frameworks or languages without team agreement.
88	- Keep the app runnable at every commit. If you break `main`, fixing it is the top priority.
89	- Document how to run anything you add (see §6) in the same commit.
90	- Use `entire agent-help` for machine-readable, version-accurate CLI usage instead of guessing commands.
91	
92	**Handing off / resuming**
93	- Use `entire session resume <branch>` or `entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>` to pick up someone else's context instead of re-deriving it.
94	- `entire dispatch` produces a summary of recent agent work — use it for handoffs and pitch prep.
95	
96	**When unsure** about requirements or the challenge brief: ask the team; challenge questions go to the partners on **Discord** (https://discord.gg/4UDNd5TAg). Do not assume partner support is available overnight.
97	
98	## 5. LLMs, keys, and resources
99	
100	- **OpenAI** is a tech partner: each participant has **75 USD** of LLM/API credits. Use them for app-level LLM calls.
101	- Keys go in a local `.env` (gitignored) and are read via environment variables; provide a `.env.example` with placeholder names only.
102	- Be mindful of token spend; `entire session tokens <id>` / `entire checkpoint tokens <id>` show usage.
103	
104	## 6. Demo & submission readiness
105

# kolosok-rehack — AI Development Guidelines

Team **Kolosok** at the **European Hackathon League (EHL) Grand Finale**, Munich (TUM.ai).
This file is the rulebook for every AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) and human working in this repo.
**Read it fully before your first change.** Human setup (GitHub token, credentials) lives in `README-Human`.

Source: [EHL Finale – All you need to know](https://tum-ai.notion.site/REDACTED)

---

## 0. Hard rules (non-negotiable)

1. **Entire must be enabled and every commit must carry a checkpoint.** The organisers will reject a submission that does not use Entire. No Entire → no valid submission.
2. **All work goes through git and gets pushed to `origin`.** Nothing that exists only on one laptop counts.
3. **`main` must always be demo-able.** We have a strict 6-minute slot for pitch + demo + questions.
4. **Never commit secrets** (API keys, tokens, `.env`). Entire redacts secrets in session logs, but do not rely on that.
5. **Never rewrite pushed history** (no `push --force`, no amending/rebasing pushed commits, no deleting `entire/*` branches or refs). Checkpoints are tied to commits; rewriting history can orphan them.

## 1. Key times (Munich local time)

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10 Oct, 11:00–11:30 | Entire technical onboarding |
| **Sat 10 Oct, 13:00** | **Challenge selection deadline** (captain, on https://ehl.gg/) |
| Sat 13:30 → Sun 12:00 | Hacking |
| **Sun 11 Oct, 12:00** | **Submission deadline** — hard stop |
| Sun 12:00–14:30 | Challenge pitches (6 min incl. Q&A) |
| Sun 15:30–16:30 | Main-stage final (6 teams) |

Internal targets: **feature freeze Sun 10:00**, first full submission by **Sun 10:30**, final re-submission by **11:45**.
Submissions can be repeated as often as we like before the deadline, so submit early and update.

**Challenge:** BMW Group — AI for Product Decision Making: an app that turns customer feedback, product/sales data and web research into prioritized, PM-reviewed customer requirements with a full audit trail. Details: [`BMW-Challenge.md`](BMW-Challenge.md).

## 2. Setup checklist (each machine, once)

Prerequisites: `git` on `PATH` (Entire shells out to it — it fails with `exec: "git": executable file not found` otherwise).

```bash
# 1. Install Entire (bash / Git Bash). On Windows the binary ends up in ~/.local/bin/entire.exe
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash

# 2. On the main branch of this repo:
git checkout main && git pull
git config pull.rebase true      # plain `git pull` makes merge commits, which carry no checkpoint
entire login                     # if not logged in yet
entire enable                    # enables session tracking in this repo
entire agent add claude-code     # install hooks for your agent; `entire agent list` shows others (codex, cursor, …)

# 3. Verify
entire status
entire doctor                    # if anything looks off
```

**You are set up correctly when** your next commit prints:

```
[entire] Pushing 1 checkpoint ref(s) to origin.... done
```

If you don't see that line, stop and fix Entire before writing more code.

## 3. Git workflow

- **Commit small and often** — at least every meaningful step, ideally every 15–30 min of agent work. Each commit becomes a checkpoint linking the code to the prompt/reasoning behind it.
- **Commit only from within a tracked agent session**, after the agent made the change with its file-edit tools. Hand-made commits, merge commits and shell (`sed`, `echo >`) edits get no checkpoint.
- **After every commit** check the checkpoint is there: `git log -1 --format=%B` must show an `Entire-Checkpoint:` line. If it is missing, fix it *before* pushing.
- **Commit messages:** imperative, prefixed by area, e.g. `feat(api): add route planner endpoint`, `fix(ui): handle empty results`, `docs: update run instructions`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `chore`, `test`, `demo`.
- **Sync before push:** `git pull --rebase` on *unpushed* local commits only, then `git push`. Resolve conflicts, never discard teammates' work.
- **Branches:** short-lived feature branches (`feat/<topic>`, `fix/<topic>`) merged back to `main` quickly (within a few hours). Trivial fixes may go straight to `main`. Do not let branches drift overnight.
- **Do not commit:** `.env`, credentials, `node_modules/`, virtualenvs, large datasets or model weights, build artifacts. Add them to `.gitignore` as soon as they appear.
- **After every push** check the `[entire] Pushing … checkpoint ref(s)` line appeared.

## 4. How agents should work here

**Before starting a task**
1. Read this README, `README-Human` and **`VISION.md`** (our product idea, shared context for everyone); look at `Concept/` for the architecture sketch (`root.drawio`).
2. `git pull` and check what others (human or agent) are doing:
   - `entire recap` — summary of recent checkpoint activity
   - `entire session list` — active/past agent sessions
   - `entire checkpoint search "<topic>"` — has someone already tried this?
3. Confirm the task is not already in progress to avoid duplicate work.

**While working**
- Keep scope tight: do the requested task, nothing more. Hackathon time is the scarcest resource.
- Prefer simple, working solutions over clever ones; a reliable demo beats extra features.
- Match existing structure, naming, and style. Don't introduce new frameworks or languages without team agreement.
- Keep the app runnable at every commit. If you break `main`, fixing it is the top priority.
- Document how to run anything you add (see §6) in the same commit.
- Use `entire agent-help` for machine-readable, version-accurate CLI usage instead of guessing commands.

**Handing off / resuming**
- Use `entire session resume <branch>` or `entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>` to pick up someone else's context instead of re-deriving it.
- `entire dispatch` produces a summary of recent agent work — use it for handoffs and pitch prep.

**When unsure** about requirements or the challenge brief: ask the team; challenge questions go to the partners on **Discord** (https://discord.gg/4UDNd5TAg). Do not assume partner support is available overnight.

## 5. LLMs, keys, and resources

- **OpenAI** is a tech partner: each participant has **75 USD** of LLM/API credits. Use them for app-level LLM calls.
- Keys go in a local `.env` (gitignored) and are read via environment variables; provide a `.env.example` with placeholder names only.
- Be mindful of token spend; `entire session tokens <id>` / `entire checkpoint tokens <id>` show usage.

## 6. Demo & submission readiness

- Judging is a **strict 6-minute slot including questions** — design the product around one clear, rehearsable demo flow.
- Keep a **"How to run"** section here up to date (install, env vars, start command, demo script).
- Before submission: everything pushed, Entire checkpoints present (`entire checkpoint list`), all relevant content uploaded on https://ehl.gg/.
- Have a fallback (recorded video or screenshots) in case the live demo fails.

### How to run

Decision graph API (Phase 1 — Postgres + the `add_node` core + the 8 agent tools from `VISION.md`):

```bash
docker compose up -d                 # Postgres on localhost:5432
cd backend
python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/activate   # (or `source .venv/bin/activate` on Linux/macOS)
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000   # creates tables on startup
```

Run tests (needs the Postgres container up): `cd backend && pytest`.

API docs once running: http://localhost:8000/docs. Endpoints: `GET /nodes`, `GET /nodes/{id}`, `GET /nodes/{id}/inputs`, `GET /nodes/{id}/dependents`, `POST /tools/{import_source,query_data,web_search,add_claim,add_assumption,propose_requirement,score,challenge,ask_pm}`, `POST /decide` (PM only). This is the data-transit contract for the GUI, agent-loop and ingestion modules.

### Agent loop (concept + runnable skeleton)

`agent-loop/README.md` has the design for the Look → Decide → Act → Pause loop from `VISION.md`.
`agent-loop/loop.py` is a thin, runnable skeleton of it: `decide()` is a stubbed rule-based
placeholder (clearly marked) for where a real LLM call goes; the rest already talks to the
real API. Run it with the backend up:

```bash
cd agent-loop
python -m venv .venv && .venv/Scripts/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python loop.py          # or: pytest (tests decide()'s logic without a server)
```

### For teammates building GUI / agent-loop / ingestion

Build against the HTTP API above, not against `backend/app/` directly — it's the one shared contract, so all three modules can be developed independently without colliding on the same Python code.

- **Base URL:** `http://localhost:8000` once the steps above are running. CORS is open (`allow_origins=["*"]`), so a browser-based GUI can call it directly.
- **Every write goes through one of the `/tools/*` endpoints or `/decide`** — there is no other way to write to the graph, by design (see `VISION.md` → "Write rules").
- **Errors:** `400` with a `{"detail": "..."}` body means a rule was rejected (missing required input, input id doesn't exist, non-PM caller on `/decide`). `404` means a `GET` asked for a node id that doesn't exist. Anything else is a bug — report it.
- **Node types, edge relations, and which tool writes what** are specified in `VISION.md` → "Data model" and "Agent tools"; the API enforces those rules server-side, so you don't need to re-check them client-side.
- **Example** (turn evidence into a claim):
  ```bash
  curl -X POST localhost:8000/tools/add_claim -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"content":{"text":"seats too narrow"},"evidence_ids":["EVD-001"],"created_by":"agent:researcher"}'
  ```
- Tests in `backend/tests/test_graph.py` double as runnable examples of every tool's expected inputs/outputs.

## 7. Repo map

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | This file — AI/dev guidelines (agents: start here) |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` | Auto-loaded agent entry points; they point here |
| `README-Human` | Human onboarding: GitHub token & credential setup |
| `BMW-Challenge.md` | BMW challenge brief: mission, scope, data, deliverables |
| `VISION.md` | Our product idea (decision graph / thought chains): read before building |
| `Concept/root.drawio` | Architecture / concept diagram |
| `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.entire/` | Entire hook config — generated by `entire enable`; do not edit by hand |

"""The real Decide step (VISION.md: "it picks its next action and stores
why"). Needs OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment (see repo root .env.example).
"""

import json
import os

from openai import OpenAI

MODEL = os.environ.get("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini")

_CONTENT = {
    "type": "object",
    "description": "the node's content. Always a JSON object, e.g. {\"text\": \"...\"} or "
                   "{\"quote\": \"...\", \"url\": \"...\"} — never a plain string.",
    "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}},
}
_IDS = {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
_RATIONALE = {"type": "string", "description": "why this action, for the node's rationale field"}

TOOLS = [
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "query_data", "description": "Look into the BMW files for evidence.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "source_ids": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
                        "required": ["content", "source_ids", "rationale"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "web_search", "description": "Find competitor info/trends; content must include a url.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "inputs": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
                        "required": ["content", "inputs", "rationale"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "add_claim", "description": "State a finding, linked to its evidence.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "evidence_ids": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
                        "required": ["content", "evidence_ids", "rationale"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "add_assumption", "description": "State a forward-looking guess, clearly marked as not evidence.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "inputs": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
                        "required": ["content", "inputs", "rationale"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "propose_requirement", "description": "Turn one or more claims into a requirement.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "claim_ids": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
                        "required": ["content", "claim_ids", "rationale"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "score", "description": "Run the fixed scoring formula on a requirement.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
            "content": _CONTENT, "target_id": {"type": "string"}, "formula": {"type": "string"},
            "rationale": _RATIONALE},
            "required": ["content", "target_id", "formula", "rationale"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "challenge", "description": "Look for counter-evidence to an existing node.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "target_id": {"type": "string"}, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
                        "required": ["content", "target_id", "rationale"]}}},
    {"type": "function", "function": {
        "name": "ask_pm", "description": "Stop and ask the PM a question when no good next step exists.",
        "parameters": {"type": "object",
                        "properties": {"content": _CONTENT, "inputs": _IDS, "rationale": _RATIONALE},
                        "required": ["content", "rationale"]}}},
]

SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are the agent building a product-decision graph (VISION.md). You are given the "
    "current graph's signals (sources without evidence, evidence without a claim, claims "
    "without a requirement, stale nodes, open questions). Pick exactly one tool call that "
    "makes the most progress right "
    "now, and fill in its 'rationale' argument explaining why. If nothing useful can be done, "
    "call ask_pm."
)


def decide_with_llm(signals: dict, client: OpenAI | None = None) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    client = client or OpenAI()
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=MODEL,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": json.dumps(signals, default=str)},
        ],
        tools=TOOLS,
        tool_choice="required",
    )
    call = resp.choices[0].message.tool_calls[0]
    args = json.loads(call.function.arguments)
    args["created_by"] = "agent:loop"
    return call.function.name, args

import json
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from llm import decide_with_llm


def test_decide_with_llm_parses_tool_call_and_stamps_created_by():
    call = MagicMock()
    call.function.name = "ask_pm"
    call.function.arguments = json.dumps({"content": {"text": "why?", "rationale": "nothing to do"}})

    resp = MagicMock()
    resp.choices[0].message.tool_calls = [call]

    client = MagicMock()
    client.chat.completions.create.return_value = resp

    tool, args = decide_with_llm({"stale": []}, client=client)

    assert tool == "ask_pm"
    assert args["created_by"] == "agent:loop"
    assert args["content"]["text"] == "why?"

from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd


def read_csv_files():
    csv_directory = Path(__file__).parent
    return {
        csv_file.stem: pd.read_csv(csv_file)
        for csv_file in csv_directory.glob("*.csv")
    }


def build_criticism_matrix(tables):
    """Count distinct defect/usability feedback IDs per vehicle part and model."""
    if not tables:
        return pd.DataFrame().rename_axis(index="Vehicle part", columns="Vehicle model")

    feedback = pd.concat(tables.values(), ignore_index=True)
    criticism = feedback.loc[
        feedback["Feedback Type"].isin(["Defect", "Difficult to Use"])
        & feedback["Vfc level2 Name"].notna()
        & feedback["Vfc level2 Name"].ne("no_class_found")
    ]
    return (
        criticism.groupby(["Vfc level2 Name", "Derivate (e-code)"])["ID"]
        .nunique()
        .unstack(fill_value=0)
        .rename_axis(index="Vehicle part", columns="Vehicle model")
    )

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """\
You are the agent building a product-decision graph for BMW product managers (PMs).
The graph grows along one chain: Source (a data file) -> Evidence (query_data: one concrete
finding from a source) -> Claim (add_claim) -> Requirement (propose_requirement) -> score.
Each turn you get the graph's signals and your recent_actions; pick exactly ONE tool call.

Rules:
1. Evidence must contain real data. For query_data, read the source's content in `sources`
   and put one specific finding in content: {"text": "<finding>", "quote": "<exact row
   text>", "source_ref": "<row reference>"}. Never write an instruction, plan or request
   ("inspect the file...") as evidence. If a source has no usable content, call ask_pm.
2. Never invent data. Claims summarize evidence; requirements build on claims.
3. Only use node ids that appear in the signals. Ids are never guessed.
4. Move down the chain: if evidence_without_claim is non-empty, prefer add_claim over another
   query_data; if claims_without_requirement is non-empty, prefer propose_requirement.
5. Read recent_actions. Do not repeat a finding you already recorded, do not retry a call
   that just errored with the same arguments, and do not pick the same tool a third time in
   a row unless it records a genuinely new finding.
6. Always fill 'rationale' with why this step, citing the ids it builds on.
7. If no step makes real progress, call ask_pm with a specific question.
8. If `required_action` is given, call exactly that tool with those ids and write its
   content and rationale.
"""


def decide_with_llm(
    signals: dict,
    history: list[dict] | None = None,
    forced: tuple[str, dict] | None = None,
    client: OpenAI | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    """forced=(tool, ids) pins the tool and its input ids (hybrid mode); the LLM then only
    writes content + rationale."""
    client = client or OpenAI()
    payload = {"signals": signals, "recent_actions": history or []}
    tool_choice = "required"
    if forced:
        tool, ids = forced
        payload["required_action"] = {"tool": tool, **ids}
        tool_choice = {"type": "function", "function": {"name": tool}}
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=MODEL,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": json.dumps(payload, default=str)},
        ],
        tools=TOOLS,
        tool_choice=tool_choice,
    )

input.new_string:
- `max_actions`: the pause budget (VISION.md: "after N actions").
- The last 5 actions of the current run (`history` in `run()`), so Decide sees its own repeats
  and rejected calls. Not kept across pauses — the graph *is* the state. Each resume re-runs
  Look from scratch, which is why stale/open-question signals must be computed from the graph,
  not from loop memory.

## Running it with data

The loop needs a Source with real content, or there is nothing to extract evidence from.
Until the ingestion module exists, seed one from a CSV (backend running):

```bash
python seed.py sample_data/demo_feedback.csv   # 12 synthetic 5 Series rows (from alex_demo1)
python loop.py                                 # needs OPENAI_API_KEY in the env for the LLM
```

## Why it used to stall (fixed)

Early live runs (gpt-4o-mini, then gpt-6-luna: 1 of 3 clean) kept calling `query_data` and
never reached a claim. Causes: the seeded Source held only a filename, so evidence was the
model's own "inspect the file" request and it rightly refused to build claims on it; Decide had
no memory of its last actions; and once a source had evidence it vanished from the signals,
so the model guessed ids. Fixed by real rows in Sources (`seed.py`), the `sources` signal plus
`inputs` on each evidence node, recent-action history, and a stricter prompt. Live result after
the fix: 8/8 actions without errors, Source → Evidence → Claim → Requirement → Score, then the
next finding.

## What's intentionally not here (teammate's call)

- Any UI/CLI

# Agent loop — design

Implements the loop from `VISION.md` → "System: how the graph gets built". Talks to the
decision-graph API only over HTTP (`backend/`'s `/tools/*`, `/decide`, `/nodes*` — see the
root `README.md`'s "For teammates" section), never imports `backend/app/` directly, so this
module can be built and run independently of the backend.

## The loop

```
Look → Decide → Act → Pause
```

1. **Look** — `GET /nodes` (or targeted subsets) and compute a few signals about the current
   graph state: which Sources have no Evidence yet, which Claims have no Requirement built on
   them, which nodes are `stale`, which Questions are still open. This is the "what's known,
   open, weak or contradictory" read VISION.md describes.
2. **Decide** — given the signals, pick exactly one next action: one of the 8 tools
   (`query_data`, `web_search`, `add_claim`, `add_assumption`, `propose_requirement`, `score`,
   `challenge`, `ask_pm`) plus its arguments, and a `rationale` string explaining why. **This is
   the one step that needs a real LLM call** — the skeleton in `loop.py` stubs it with a fixed
   priority rule so the rest of the loop is runnable and testable today.
3. **Act** — call the chosen tool's endpoint. The API is the single write path, so a failed
   call (400) means the decision was invalid (e.g. a dangling input id) — log it and let Decide
   pick something else next iteration, don't crash the loop.
4. **Pause** — stop after `max_actions` iterations, or immediately if Decide's only option was
   `ask_pm`, and hand a summary of what was written back to the PM. The PM reviews/steers via
   `POST /decide` on any node Act created; nothing here auto-applies a PM's changes — VISION.md
   says stale propagation and re-review are the next loop's job, not this one's.

## State the loop needs between pauses

- `max_actions`: the pause budget (VISION.md: "after N actions").
- Nothing else needs to persist in the loop process itself — the graph *is* the state. Each
  resume re-runs Look from scratch, which is why stale/open-question signals must be computed
  from the graph, not from loop memory.

## Known limitation (observed in a live test run)

With `gpt-4o-mini`, Decide sometimes keeps calling `query_data` for the same source instead of
moving on to `add_claim` once evidence already exists — the `evidence_without_claim` signal is
there, but the model doesn't always act on it. The loop itself doesn't break (a rejected call
now logs an error and lets Decide try again, see `act()`), so this is prompt-quality tuning,
not a correctness bug. Worth revisiting the system prompt or trying a stronger model if it
matters for the demo.

## What's intentionally not here (teammate's call)

- The real Decide step (LLM prompt, tool-call parsing) — `loop.py`'s `decide()` is a stub, see
  its `shortcut:` comment.
- Any UI/CLI for the PM to review a pause's summary — that's the GUI module's job; this loop
  just returns/prints the summary.
- Detecting "PM answered a Question" to resume faster — out of scope for the first pass; Look
  re-reading the whole graph each time covers it for now.

I made all five changes (A, B, C, F and the stricter prompt) on a new branch, `feat/agent-loop-unstall`. In a live run with gpt-4o-mini the loop no longer stalls. Nothing is committed or pushed yet; the commands for both steps are at the bottom.

## Step 1: push the LLM feature to `dev`
`dev` is an ancestor of `feat/agent-loop-llm`, so this is a fast-forward. No merge commit is created and the existing checkpoints stay as they are. That branch doesn't include anything from the gpt-6-luna trials: that code only lived in the trial script, which I deleted.

## Step 2: what changed

| | Change |
|---|---|
| **A** | `seed.py` imports a CSV as a Source node that carries its rows. `sample_data/demo_feedback.csv` is an exact copy of the 12 synthetic 5 Series rows from teammate branch `alex_demo1`. The real BMW data isn't anywhere in the repo or on this machine. |
| **B** | `run()` passes the last 5 actions, including rejected calls, to the model on each decision. |
| **C** | The signals now include a `sources` list with each source's content, and each unclaimed evidence node lists its `inputs`. The model no longer has to guess ids. |
| **F** | `DECIDE_MODE=hybrid`: the fixed rules pick the tool and input ids, and the LLM only writes the content and rationale. |
| **Prompt** | 8 explicit rules: evidence must quote real data, ids only from the signals, move down the chain, no repeats, specific questions when asking the PM. |

All 8 agent-loop tests pass, including new ones for the hybrid merge and for passing the forced tool and history to the model.

**Live results (gpt-4o-mini, seeded demo CSV):**
- **`llm` mode:** 8 of 8 actions with no errors. It went Evidence → Claim → Requirement → Score on the voice-assistant complaint, then picked up the next real finding (navigation charging) and the one after (app lag). Every evidence node quotes an actual row with its `source_ref`.
- **`hybrid` mode:** 4 clean steps, from Evidence through Requirement to a specific question for the PM. It stops early because the fixed rules allow only one `query_data` per source, so it uses one finding per file. That's documented in `agent-loop/README.md`.

**Quality problems still open:**
- The Score node only repeats the requirement text; it doesn't contain an actual score.
- Requirements are worded vaguely ("requires improvements to…").

```bash
# Step 1: fast-forward dev to the LLM feature and push (fails safely if it isn't a fast-forward)
git fetch origin

"""Throwaway: 1 run per model x DECIDE_MODE, with token usage and quote-fidelity checks."""
import csv, json, os, subprocess, sys

REPO = r"C:\Users\Alex\HAckAI\kolosok-rehack"
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "agent-loop"))
import openai, llm, loop, seed  # noqa: E402

CSV = os.path.join(REPO, "agent-loop", "sample_data", "demo_feedback.csv")
ROW_TEXTS = {r["text_or_value"] for r in csv.DictReader(open(CSV, encoding="utf-8"))}
usage = {"in": 0, "out": 0}


class Client:
    def __init__(self, model):
        self._c, self._model = openai.OpenAI(), model
        self.chat = self
        self.completions = self

    def create(self, **kw):
        if self._model.startswith("gpt-6"):
            kw["reasoning_effort"] = "none"  # luna rejects tools otherwise
        resp = self._c.chat.completions.create(**kw)
        usage["in"] += resp.usage.prompt_tokens
        usage["out"] += resp.usage.completion_tokens
        return resp


def reset():
    subprocess.run(["docker", "compose", "exec", "-T", "db", "psql", "-q", "-U", "kolosok",
                    "-d", "decision_graph", "-c",
                    "TRUNCATE edges, nodes CASCADE; UPDATE node_counters SET next = 1;"],
                   cwd=REPO, check=True, capture_output=True)


out = []
for model in ["gpt-4o-mini", "gpt-6-luna"]:
    for mode in ["llm", "hybrid"]:
        reset()
        seed.seed(CSV)
        llm.MODEL = model
        llm.OpenAI = lambda m=model: Client(m)
        os.environ["DECIDE_MODE"] = mode
        usage.update({"in": 0, "out": 0})
        actions = []
        for r in loop.run(max_actions=8):
            c = r.get("content") or {}
            actions.append({"id": r.get("id"), "error": r.get("error"),
                            "text": c.get("text"), "quote": c.get("quote"),
                            "quote_exact": c.get("quote") in ROW_TEXTS if c.get("quote") else None,
                            "content_keys": sorted(c), "rationale": r.get("rationale")})
        nodes = loop.requests.get(f"{loop.API_BASE}/nodes").json()
        edges = {n["id"]: [i["id"] for i in loop.requests.get(
            f"{loop.API_BASE}/nodes/{n['id']}/inputs").json()] for n in nodes}
        out.append({"model": model, "mode": mode, "tokens_in": usage["in"],
                    "tokens_out": usage["out"], "actions": actions, "edges": edges})
        print(model, mode, "done", usage, flush=True)

reset()
json.dump(out, open(sys.argv[1], "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

content.text:
# Agent loop evaluation: 2 models × 2 decision modes

I read "1 run per tool" as one run for each combination: gpt-4o-mini and gpt-6-luna, each in `llm` mode (the model picks every step) and `hybrid` mode (fixed rules pick the step, the model writes the content). That's 4 runs on the seeded 12-row demo CSV, each starting from an empty database, with an 8-action limit. All 4 ran cleanly: no stalls, no errors, no guessed ids, and every graph link points to a real node.

| Run | Actions | Graph built | Tokens in / out | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4o-mini · llm | 8 | 3 findings → 2 claims → 2 requirements → 1 score | 21,177 / 720 | $0.0036 |
| 4o-mini · hybrid | 4 | 1 finding → 1 claim → 1 requirement → question to PM | 10,907 / 342 | $0.0018 |
| **luna · llm** | 8 | 3 findings → 3 claims → 2 requirements | 22,487 / 878 | **$0.0027** |
| luna · hybrid | 4 | 1 finding → 1 claim → 1 requirement → question to PM | 11,326 / 425 | $0.0013 |

All 4 runs together cost about $0.009. luna is roughly 25% cheaper than 4o-mini for the same work.

## What works now
- **Evidence is real data.** 7 of the 8 evidence nodes quote a CSV row exactly. The 8th (luna, hybrid) quotes the whole CSV line with the columns joined together; the content is right, just not word for word.
- **The chain moves forward on its own.** Both models in `llm` mode followed the order evidence → claim → requirement, then went back for a different row. Neither repeated a finding.

## Quality: luna is clearly better
- **luna's requirements are more specific.** For example: *"Improve … recognition of place names … and validate recognition performance with representative in-car utterances."* gpt-4o-mini wrote *"needs improvement in understanding…"* and *"There should be improved features for electric range…"*.
- **luna's rationales are better.** They cite node ids and explain why a step isn't a repeat: *"complements, but does not repeat, the long-trip planning claim CLM-002"*.
- **gpt-4o-mini overclaims and copies.** From one dealer-trend row it claimed a *"growing customer concern"*. In hybrid mode its claim was a word-for-word copy of the evidence.

## Problems found (both models)

| # | Problem | Evidence | Possible fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Scoring doesn't exist.** The score tool has no real formula behind it. | 4o-mini's score node only restates the requirement. Both hybrid runs stopped to ask the PM *"what criteria should we use for scoring?"* | Define the scoring formula. Ideally it uses the CSV's `reliability` column, which no run used. This is a backend task. |
| 2 | **No consolidation.** Every claim rests on exactly one row, so every requirement has n=1 evidence. | Rows 2, 8 and 11 are all about charging. luna saw the link but still made a separate claim. | Prompt: "if a new finding supports an existing theme, add it to that claim's evidence". Or extract all evidence first, then group it. |
| 3 | **The `quote` field gets misused.** Models put their own text in `quote` on requirements and questions, which looks like a citation but isn't. | 4o-mini hybrid: REQ-001 and QST-001 "quote" themselves. | Offer the `quote` and `source_ref` fields only on `query_data`'s content. |
| 4 | **Questions to the PM aren't linked to what they're about.** | Both QST-001 nodes have no inputs, though each asks about REQ-001. | Make the fixed rules pass the relevant ids to `ask_pm`, or let the model fill `inputs` in hybrid mode. |
| 5 | **Hybrid mode stops after one finding per file**, as documented. | 4 steps, then a question to the PM. | Only fixable by giving the rules a "more rows left" signal. |
| 6 | **Input tokens grow with the source size.** Each step's request includes about 2.7k input tokens, mostly the full CSV. | 12 rows already account for most of it; the real customer feedback would blow past the context window. | Chunking (already marked as a shortcut in the code). |

## Recommendation
**Make gpt-6-luna in `llm` mode the default.** It's cheaper and produces better requirements. To switch, `llm.py` needs `reasoning_effort="none"` when the model is luna. I passed it from the test runner only, so the shipped code can't run luna as-is.

After that, I'd fix #1 (scoring) and #2 (consolidation) first: they decide whether the result looks like real prioritized requirements or a list of single-verbatim paraphrases. #3 and #4 are small cleanups.

Want me to do the luna switch plus #3 and #4 now, and take #1 and #2 as a separate step?

This is one run per combination, so it's indicative rather than statistical. The demo data is synthetic and tidy, so the real BMW customer feedback will be harder. The test runner stays in the scratchpad, nothing in the repo changed, and the database has been reset.

## Evaluation (2026-10-11) — 1 run per model × mode

Setup: fresh DB, `seed.py sample_data/demo_feedback.csv`, `run(max_actions=8)`.

| Model · mode | Actions | Graph built | Tokens in / out | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-4o-mini · llm | 8 | 3 EVD → 2 CLM → 2 REQ → 1 SCR | 21,177 / 720 | $0.0036 |
| gpt-4o-mini · hybrid | 4 | 1 EVD → 1 CLM → 1 REQ → QST | 10,907 / 342 | $0.0018 |
| **gpt-6-luna · llm** | 8 | 3 EVD → 3 CLM → 2 REQ | 22,487 / 878 | **$0.0027** |
| gpt-6-luna · hybrid | 4 | 1 EVD → 1 CLM → 1 REQ → QST | 11,326 / 425 | $0.0013 |

Prices: gpt-6-luna $0.10 / $0.50 per M tokens in/out, gpt-4o-mini $0.15 / $0.60 (third-party
listings — check OpenAI's pricing page). One run each, so indicative, not statistical.

What works: no stalls, 0 errors and 0 guessed ids in 24 actions; 7/8 evidence quotes match a
CSV row exactly; both models walk the chain unprompted and pick a new row each time.

Quality: **gpt-6-luna is clearly better** — testable requirements ("…validate recognition
performance with representative in-car utterances") and rationales that cite ids. gpt-4o-mini
writes vague requirements ("needs improvement…"), overclaims ("growing customer concern" from a
single row), and in hybrid mode copied the evidence verbatim into the claim.

**Recommendation:** default to gpt-6-luna in `llm` mode. It needs `reasoning_effort="none"`
on the `chat.completions.create()` call in `llm.py` (otherwise OpenAI rejects tool calls with
a 400) — not in the code yet; the evaluation passed it from a throwaway runner.

## Open problems (for whoever picks this up)

Ordered by impact on the demo. 1–2 decide whether the output looks like prioritized
requirements or a list of one-verbatim paraphrases.

1. **Scoring isn't defined.** `score` takes a free-text `formula` and nothing computes a
   score — 4o-mini's SCR node just restated the requirement, and both hybrid runs paused to ask
   the PM "what scoring criteria?". Needs a real formula (VISION.md: "fixed scoring formula"),
   ideally backend-side. The CSV's `reliability` column (0.72–0.92) is a ready input that no run
   used.
2. **No consolidation — every requirement rests on one row.** Each claim links exactly one
   evidence node. Rows 2, 8 and 11 are all about charging; luna noticed the connection but still
   made a separate claim. Options: prompt rule "if a finding supports an existing claim's theme,
   claim across several evidence_ids", or a two-phase run (extract all evidence, then group).
3. **`quote` field misused outside Evidence.** Requirements and Questions sometimes put the
   model's own text in `quote`, which reads like a citation. Fix: separate `_CONTENT` schemas —
   `quote`/`source_ref` only on `query_data`.
4. **Questions aren't linked to what they ask about.** Both QST-001 nodes have no inputs
   though they ask about REQ-001. Fix: `decide_rule_based()`'s `ask_pm` passes the relevant ids,
   or hybrid lets the LLM fill `inputs`.
5. **Hybrid extracts one finding per file**, because `sources_without_evidence` empties after
   the first `query_data`. Needs a "rows left unprocessed" signal if hybrid should go deeper.
6. **Prompt size grows with the source.** ~2.7k input tokens per call for 12 rows, mostly the
   CSV (`sources` signal in `look()`, marked `shortcut:`). Real verbatim files need chunking or
   per-call row selection before they're seeded.
7. **Unused tools.** No run called `web_search`, `challenge` or `add_assumption` — Look has no
   signal that would trigger them (e.g. "requirement with only one evidence" → `challenge`).

# Agent loop — design

Implements the loop from `VISION.md` → "System: how the graph gets built". Talks to the
decision-graph API only over HTTP (`backend/`'s `/tools/*`, `/decide`, `/nodes*` — see the
root `README.md`'s "For teammates" section), never imports `backend/app/` directly, so this
module can be built and run independently of the backend.

## The loop

```
Look → Decide → Act → Pause
```

1. **Look** — `GET /nodes` (or targeted subsets) and compute a few signals about the current
   graph state: which Sources have no Evidence yet, which Claims have no Requirement built on
   them, which nodes are `stale`, which Questions are still open. This is the "what's known,
   open, weak or contradictory" read VISION.md describes.
2. **Decide** — given the signals and this run's recent actions, pick exactly one next
   action: one of the 8 tools (`query_data`, `web_search`, `add_claim`, `add_assumption`,
   `propose_requirement`, `score`, `challenge`, `ask_pm`) plus its arguments, and a `rationale`
   string explaining why. `llm.py` does this with OpenAI tool-calling; `DECIDE_MODE` picks how:
   - `llm` (default): the LLM picks the tool and writes everything.
   - `hybrid`: `decide_rule_based()` picks the tool and input ids (guaranteed progress), the
     LLM only writes content + rationale. Limit: only one `query_data` per source, so it
     extracts one finding per file and then walks that finding to `ask_pm`.
   - No `OPENAI_API_KEY`: `decide_rule_based()` alone (tests, offline).
3. **Act** — call the chosen tool's endpoint. The API is the single write path, so a failed
   call (400) means the decision was invalid (e.g. a dangling input id) — log it and let Decide
   pick something else next iteration, don't crash the loop.
4. **Pause** — stop after `max_actions` iterations, or immediately if Decide's only option was
   `ask_pm`, and hand a summary of what was written back to the PM. The PM reviews/steers via
   `POST /decide` on any node Act created; nothing here auto-applies a PM's changes — VISION.md
   says stale propagation and re-review are the next loop's job, not this one's.

## State the loop needs between pauses

- `max_actions`: the pause budget (VISION.md: "after N actions").
- The last 5 actions of the current run (`history` in `run()`), so Decide sees its own repeats
  and rejected calls. Not kept across pauses — the graph *is* the state. Each resume re-runs
  Look from scratch, which is why stale/open-question signals must be computed from the graph,
  not from loop memory.

## Running it with data

The loop needs a Source with real content, or there is nothing to extract evidence from.
Until the ingestion module exists, seed one from a CSV (backend running):

```bash
python seed.py sample_data/demo_feedback.csv   # 12 synthetic 5 Series rows (from alex_demo1)
python loop.py                                 # needs OPENAI_API_KEY in the env for the LLM
```

## Why it used to stall (fixed)

Early live runs (gpt-4o-mini, then gpt-6-luna: 1 of 3 clean) kept calling `query_data` and
never reached a claim. Causes: the seeded Source held only a filename, so evidence was the
model's own "inspect the file" request and it rightly refused to build claims on it; Decide had
no memory of its last actions; and once a source had evidence it vanished from the signals,

`inputs` on each evidence node, recent-action history, and a stricter prompt. Live result after
the fix: 8/8 actions without errors, Source → Evidence → Claim → Requirement → Score, then the
next finding.

- Any UI/CLI for the PM to review a pause's summary — that's the GUI module's job; this loop
  just returns/prints the summary.
- Detecting "PM answered a Question" to resume faster — out of scope for the first pass; Look
  re-reading the whole graph each time covers it for now.

85-2. **Append-only:** nodes are never changed or deleted. An edit creates a new version that points to the old one (`replaces`). The full history is therefore always kept, and that history is the audit trail.
86-3. **Every node except Source, Question and Note must have inputs**, so nothing is untraceable.
87:4. **Readable over exhaustive:** one Source node per file, not per row. Evidence keeps its quotes/rows inside its content, so the graph stays small enough for a person to keep an overview.
88-5. **Human-only nodes:** Decisions and prioritisation weights can only be created by the PM. This is enforced inside `add_node` (it rejects them unless `created_by` is a PM), not in the prompt.

121-- **The agent** gets "these nodes are stale because of X" as its next task and decides what to redo, drop or keep.
122:- **PM decisions** are never changed automatically; they are flagged "re-review: evidence changed".

1	# Vision — Decision Graph (database of thought chains)
2	
3	> The team's shared starting idea. Every agent and teammate should read this before working on the product.
4	> Challenge context: [`BMW-Challenge.md`](BMW-Challenge.md). Status: **idea stage, details still open.**
5	
6	## The problem
7	
8	A product manager (PM) defining the next vehicle generation works with many sources of information:
9	market analysis, conferences, sales figures, customer feedback and more. **These sources are not connected to each other.**
10	The path from "what we know" to "what we decided" lives in people's heads, slides and meetings. Afterwards it is hard to see
11	**how and why** a decision was made.
12	
13	## Our central idea
14	
15	This is the main innovation of our solution.

# Vision — Decision Graph (database of thought chains)

> The team's shared starting idea. Every agent and teammate should read this before working on the product.
> Challenge context: [`BMW-Challenge.md`](BMW-Challenge.md). Status: **idea stage, details still open.**

## The problem

A product manager (PM) defining the next vehicle generation works with many sources of information:
market analysis, conferences, sales figures, customer feedback and more. **These sources are not connected to each other.**
The path from "what we know" to "what we decided" lives in people's heads, slides and meetings. Afterwards it is hard to see
**how and why** a decision was made.

## Our central idea

This is the main innovation of our solution.

A tool that lets the PM arrive at a new specification (a set of requirements, i.e. the solution) **by reasoning it out step by step**.
The emphasis is on **interpretability**: the system must show its reasoning, not just give answers.

**Data structure: a database of thought chains.**
It is inspired by git and graphs; the comparison is loose, not literal.

- **What:** a structure that records **how and why each step of a decision was made**.
- **Why:** to make the decision process **explainable and transparent**.
- **How:** every meeting, agent call, tool run, report and so on creates a **node**. Nodes connect to the nodes they came from or depend on.
  Over time these nodes form a **graph** that anyone can examine to trace a decision back to its origins.

## Bigger ambition (feasibility not yet decided)

Our first idea was an app that **automates the decision-making process end to end**:
a workflow takes the PM's requests and works step by step toward a decision, using tools, agents and so on.
Every step would be recorded as nodes in the graph.

In that setup the chain also becomes a control mechanism, not only a record:

- The PM can **go back to any earlier step**,
- **change an argument or a prioritisation** there,
- and that change **propagates forward** through all the steps that depend on it, updating the end result.

**Open question:** we don't know yet how feasible this is in the hackathon time frame, or which part of it we should build.
Treat this section as the direction, not a committed scope.

## Data model (agreed)

**Core rule:** the graph does no work; it only stores results.
All work happens in **processing steps** (LLM agent, formula, PM action).
**Each step run writes one new node, plus edges to the nodes it used as input.**

### Node types

| Type | What it is | Typically made by |
|---|---|---|
| **Source** | One input data file / document (e.g. "G70 feedback.xlsx") | import step |
| **Evidence** | A tool result: data query output, web search result (with URL), counter-evidence. Stores the exact quotes/rows/URLs | agent tool |
| **Claim** | A finding (complaint, unmet need, competitor gap, trend), linked to its evidence | agent or PM |
| **Assumption** | A forward-looking guess (3–5 years), explicitly marked as not evidence | agent or PM |
| **Question** | An open question: from the agent to the PM, or a PM instruction to the agent | agent or PM |
| **Requirement** | A customer requirement proposal | agent or PM |
| **Score** | Priority score with its formula breakdown | scoring formula |
| **Decision** | PM approves / rejects / postpones / edits **any** node, with reason | **PM only** |
| **Note** | Free input: meeting outcome, expert opinion, PM comment | PM / team |

### Fields

```
Node
  id           e.g. "CLM-012"
  type         Source | Evidence | Claim | Assumption | Question | Requirement | Score | Decision | Note
  content      the result itself
  created_by   "agent:<name>" | "tool:<name>" | "PM:<name>"
  method       prompt or formula used
  rationale    why (LLM explanation or PM comment)
  timestamp
  version      1, 2, 3 …
  replaces     id of the previous version (empty for v1)
  status       ok | stale

Edge
  from, to, relation: derived_from | supports | contradicts | scores | decides
```

### Write rules

1. **Only one write function** (`add_node(type, content, inputs, created_by, method, rationale)`). Nothing else writes to the graph.
2. **Append-only:** nodes are never changed or deleted. An edit creates a new version that points to the old one (`replaces`). The full history is therefore always kept, and that history is the audit trail.
3. **Every node except Source, Question and Note must have inputs**, so nothing is untraceable.
4. **Readable over exhaustive:** one Source node per file, not per row. Evidence keeps its quotes/rows inside its content, so the graph stays small enough for a person to keep an overview.
5. **Human-only nodes:** Decisions and prioritisation weights can only be created by the PM. This is enforced inside `add_node` (it rejects them unless `created_by` is a PM), not in the prompt.

## System: how the graph gets built (agreed)

### The loop: a flexible agent, not a fixed workflow

1. **Look:** the agent reads the current graph (what's known, open, weak or contradictory).
2. **Decide:** it picks its next action and stores why (as the new node's rationale).
3. **Act:** it calls a tool; the result is written as new nodes.
4. **Pause:** after N actions, or when it needs input, it hands over to the PM.

### Agent tools

| Tool | What it does | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| `query_data` | Look into the BMW files (feedback, sales, study, equipment) | Evidence |
| `web_search` | Find competitor info and trends | Evidence (with URL) |
| `add_claim` | State a finding, linked to its evidence | Claim |
| `add_assumption` | State a forward-looking guess, clearly marked | Assumption |
| `propose_requirement` | Turn claims into a requirement | Requirement |
| `score` | Run the fixed scoring formula | Score |
| `challenge` | Look for counter-evidence to an existing node | Evidence (`contradicts`) |
| `ask_pm` | Stop and ask the PM a question | Question |

### The PM steers at any time

Accept, reject or edit any node, say "dig deeper here" or "challenge this", or give a new direction.
PM input becomes the agent's next priority.

### Going back (propagation)

When the PM changes a node, everything built on it is marked **stale**. Then:
- **Scores** recompute automatically.
- **The agent** gets "these nodes are stale because of X" as its next task and decides what to redo, drop or keep.
- **PM decisions** are never changed automatically; they are flagged "re-review: evidence changed".

**In one line:** the agent builds the reasoning, the PM steers and decides, and every step is a traceable node.

Based on this, I'm proposing a five-phase build: a read-only skeleton, PM review tools, a trace/graph view, agent control with audit logging, then demo polish.

1	-- Decision graph schema (append-only Node/Edge model, see VISION.md).
2	
3	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS nodes (
4	    id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
5	    type       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (type IN (
6	        'Source', 'Evidence', 'Claim', 'Assumption', 'Question',
7	        'Requirement', 'Score', 'Decision', 'Note'
8	    )),
9	    content    JSONB NOT NULL,
10	    created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
11	    method     TEXT,
12	    rationale  TEXT,
13	    timestamp  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
14	    version    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
15	    replaces   TEXT REFERENCES nodes(id),
16	    status     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ok' CHECK (status IN ('ok', 'stale'))
17	);
18	
19	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS edges (
20	    id       SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
21	    from_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id),
22	    to_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id),
23	    relation TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (relation IN (
24	        'derived_from', 'supports', 'contradicts', 'scores', 'decides'
25	    ))
26	);
27	
28	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_edges_from ON edges(from_id);
29	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_edges_to ON edges(to_id);
30	
31	-- Atomic per-type id counters: a row-level UPDATE lock makes concurrent
32	-- add_node() calls for the same type get distinct, gapless ids instead of
33	-- racing on a SELECT count(*) in application code.
34	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS node_counters (
35	    type TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
36	    next INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
37	);
38	
39	INSERT INTO node_counters (type) VALUES
40	    ('Source'), ('Evidence'), ('Claim'), ('Assumption'), ('Question'),
41	    ('Requirement'), ('Score'), ('Decision'), ('Note')
42	ON CONFLICT (type) DO NOTHING;
43	
44	-- Append-only enforcement: nodes can never be deleted; the only column an
45	-- UPDATE may ever touch is `status` (stale propagation, see VISION.md
46	-- "Going back (propagation)"). Everything else is a new row via add_node.
47	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION nodes_block_mutation() RETURNS trigger AS $$
48	BEGIN
49	    IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
50	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'nodes are append-only: delete not allowed';
51	    END IF;
52	    IF NEW.id <> OLD.id OR NEW.type <> OLD.type
53	        OR NEW.content IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.content
54	        OR NEW.created_by <> OLD.created_by
55	        OR NEW.method IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.method
56	        OR NEW.rationale IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.rationale
57	        OR NEW.timestamp <> OLD.timestamp
58	        OR NEW.version <> OLD.version
59	        OR NEW.replaces IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.replaces THEN
60	        RAISE EXCEPTION 'nodes are append-only: only status may change';
61	    END IF;
62	    RETURN NEW;
63	END;
64	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
65	
66	DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS nodes_append_only ON nodes;
67	CREATE TRIGGER nodes_append_only
68	    BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON nodes
69	    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION nodes_block_mutation();
70	
71	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION edges_block_mutation() RETURNS trigger AS $$
72	BEGIN
73	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'edges are append-only: update/delete not allowed';
74	END;
75	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
76	
77	DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS edges_append_only ON edges;
78	CREATE TRIGGER edges_append_only
79	    BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON edges
80	    FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION edges_block_mutation();
81

"""The decision graph's only write path (VISION.md "Write rules").

Nothing else is allowed to write nodes or edges — every agent tool and PM
action goes through add_node().
"""

from typing import Any, Optional

import psycopg
from psycopg.types.json import Json

from .db import dict_cursor, get_conn
from .models import ID_PREFIX, NO_INPUT_REQUIRED, Node, NodeType, Relation


def _next_id(cur, node_type: NodeType) -> str:
    prefix = ID_PREFIX[node_type]
    cur.execute(
        "UPDATE node_counters SET next = next + 1 WHERE type = %s RETURNING next - 1 AS n",
        (node_type.value,),
    )
    n = cur.fetchone()["n"]
    return f"{prefix}-{n:03d}"


def _row_to_node(row: dict[str, Any]) -> Node:
    return Node(**row)


def add_node(
    type: NodeType,
    content: dict[str, Any],
    inputs: list[str],
    created_by: str,
    method: Optional[str] = None,
    rationale: Optional[str] = None,
    relation: Relation = Relation.DERIVED_FROM,
    replaces: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Node:
    """Write one new node, plus edges to the nodes it used as input.

    inputs: ids of nodes this one is derived from/scores/contradicts/decides.
    relation: the edge relation used for every (new_node -> input) edge.
    replaces: id of the node this is a new version of (versioning).
    """
    node_type = NodeType(type)

    if node_type == NodeType.DECISION and not created_by.startswith("PM:"):
        raise PermissionError("Decision nodes can only be created by the PM")

    if node_type not in NO_INPUT_REQUIRED and not inputs:
        raise ValueError(f"{node_type.value} nodes must have inputs")

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            version = 1
            if replaces:
                cur.execute("SELECT version FROM nodes WHERE id = %s", (replaces,))
                prev = cur.fetchone()
                if prev is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"replaces target {replaces} does not exist")
                version = prev["version"] + 1

            node_id = _next_id(cur, node_type)
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO nodes (id, type, content, created_by, method, rationale, version, replaces)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (node_id, node_type.value, Json(content), created_by, method, rationale, version, replaces),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()

            for input_id in inputs:
                try:
                    cur.execute(
                        "INSERT INTO edges (from_id, to_id, relation) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)",
                        (node_id, input_id, relation.value),
                    )
                except psycopg.errors.ForeignKeyViolation:
                    raise ValueError(f"input node {input_id} does not exist")

            if replaces:
                _mark_stale(cur, replaces)

    return _row_to_node(row)


def _mark_stale(cur, node_id: str) -> None:
    """Propagate staleness to every node that (transitively) depends on node_id."""
    seen = {node_id}
    frontier = [node_id]
    while frontier:
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT from_id FROM edges WHERE to_id = ANY(%s)",
            (frontier,),
        )
        next_frontier = [r["from_id"] for r in cur.fetchall() if r["from_id"] not in seen]
        seen.update(next_frontier)
        frontier = next_frontier

    cur.execute(
        "UPDATE nodes SET status = 'stale' WHERE id = ANY(%s)",
        (list(seen),),
    )


def get_node(node_id: str) -> Optional[Node]:
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE id = %s", (node_id,))
            row = cur.fetchone()
    return _row_to_node(row) if row else None


def list_nodes(type: Optional[NodeType] = None) -> list[Node]:
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            if type:
                cur.execute("SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE type = %s ORDER BY timestamp", (NodeType(type).value,))
            else:
                cur.execute("SELECT * FROM nodes ORDER BY timestamp")
            rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [_row_to_node(r) for r in rows]


def get_inputs(node_id: str) -> list[Node]:
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT n.* FROM nodes n
                JOIN edges e ON e.to_id = n.id
                WHERE e.from_id = %s
                """,
                (node_id,),
            )
            rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [_row_to_node(r) for r in rows]


def get_dependents(node_id: str) -> list[Node]:
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT n.* FROM nodes n
                JOIN edges e ON e.from_id = n.id
                WHERE e.to_id = %s
                """,
                (node_id,),
            )
            rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [_row_to_node(r) for r in rows]

"""The decision graph's only write path (VISION.md "Write rules").

Nothing else is allowed to write nodes or edges — every agent tool and PM
action goes through add_node().
"""

from typing import Any, Optional

import psycopg
from psycopg.types.json import Json

from .db import dict_cursor, get_conn
from .models import ID_PREFIX, NO_INPUT_REQUIRED, Node, NodeType, Relation


def _next_id(cur, node_type: NodeType) -> str:
    prefix = ID_PREFIX[node_type]
    cur.execute(
        "UPDATE node_counters SET next = next + 1 WHERE type = %s RETURNING next - 1 AS n",
        (node_type.value,),
    )
    n = cur.fetchone()["n"]
    return f"{prefix}-{n:03d}"


def _row_to_node(row: dict[str, Any]) -> Node:
    return Node(**row)


def add_node(
    type: NodeType,
    content: dict[str, Any],
    inputs: list[str],
    created_by: str,
    method: Optional[str] = None,
    rationale: Optional[str] = None,
    relation: Relation = Relation.DERIVED_FROM,
    replaces: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Node:
    """Write one new node, plus edges to the nodes it used as input.

    inputs: ids of nodes this one is derived from/scores/contradicts/decides.
    relation: the edge relation used for every (new_node -> input) edge.
    replaces: id of the node this is a new version of (versioning).
    """
    node_type = NodeType(type)

    if node_type == NodeType.DECISION and not created_by.startswith("PM:"):
        raise PermissionError("Decision nodes can only be created by the PM")

    if node_type not in NO_INPUT_REQUIRED and not inputs:
        raise ValueError(f"{node_type.value} nodes must have inputs")

    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            version = 1
            if replaces:
                cur.execute("SELECT version FROM nodes WHERE id = %s", (replaces,))
                prev = cur.fetchone()
                if prev is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"replaces target {replaces} does not exist")
                version = prev["version"] + 1

            node_id = _next_id(cur, node_type)
            cur.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO nodes (id, type, content, created_by, method, rationale, version, replaces)
                VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s)
                RETURNING *
                """,
                (node_id, node_type.value, Json(content), created_by, method, rationale, version, replaces),
            )
            row = cur.fetchone()

            for input_id in inputs:
                try:
                    cur.execute(
                        "INSERT INTO edges (from_id, to_id, relation) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)",
                        (node_id, input_id, relation.value),
                    )
                except psycopg.errors.ForeignKeyViolation:
                    raise ValueError(f"input node {input_id} does not exist")

            if replaces:
                _mark_stale(cur, replaces)

    return _row_to_node(row)


def _mark_stale(cur, node_id: str) -> None:
    """Propagate staleness to every node that (transitively) depends on node_id."""
    seen = {node_id}
    frontier = [node_id]
    while frontier:
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT from_id FROM edges WHERE to_id = ANY(%s)",
            (frontier,),
        )
        next_frontier = [r["from_id"] for r in cur.fetchall() if r["from_id"] not in seen]
        seen.update(next_frontier)
        frontier = next_frontier

    cur.execute(
        "UPDATE nodes SET status = 'stale' WHERE id = ANY(%s)",
        (list(seen),),
    )


def get_node(node_id: str) -> Optional[Node]:
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            cur.execute("SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE id = %s", (node_id,))
            row = cur.fetchone()
    return _row_to_node(row) if row else None


def list_nodes(type: Optional[NodeType] = None) -> list[Node]:
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            if type:
                cur.execute("SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE type = %s ORDER BY timestamp", (NodeType(type).value,))
            else:
                cur.execute("SELECT * FROM nodes ORDER BY timestamp")
            rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [_row_to_node(r) for r in rows]


def get_inputs(node_id: str) -> list[Node]:
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT n.* FROM nodes n
                JOIN edges e ON e.to_id = n.id
                WHERE e.from_id = %s
                """,
                (node_id,),
            )
            rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [_row_to_node(r) for r in rows]


def get_dependents(node_id: str) -> list[Node]:
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with dict_cursor(conn) as cur:
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT n.* FROM nodes n
                JOIN edges e ON e.from_id = n.id
                WHERE e.to_id = %s
                """,
                (node_id,),
            )
            rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [_row_to_node(r) for r in rows]

def test_end_to_end_requirement_traces_to_source():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "G70 feedback.xlsx"}, [], "tool:import")
    evidence = tools.query_data({"row": "seat too narrow"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    claim = tools.add_claim({"text": "seats too narrow for tall drivers"}, [evidence.id], "agent:researcher")
    requirement = tools.propose_requirement({"text": "widen seat by 2cm"}, [claim.id], "agent:researcher")

    scored = tools.score({"value": 7.5, "breakdown": {}}, requirement.id, "impact*reach", "formula:scoring_v1")
    decision = tools.decide({"verdict": "approve"}, requirement.id, "PM:alex", rationale="matches strategy")

    from app.graph import get_inputs

    assert get_inputs(requirement.id)[0].id == claim.id
    assert get_inputs(claim.id)[0].id == evidence.id
    assert get_inputs(evidence.id)[0].id == src.id
    assert scored.type == NodeType.SCORE
    assert decision.created_by.startswith("PM:")

def test_pm_edit_creates_new_version_with_same_inputs_and_marks_dependents_stale():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    evidence = tools.query_data({"row": "complaint"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    claim = tools.add_claim({"text": "v1"}, [evidence.id], "agent:researcher")
    requirement = tools.propose_requirement({"text": "req"}, [claim.id], "agent:researcher")

    edited = tools.edit({"text": "v2"}, claim.id, "PM:alex", rationale="sharper wording")

    from app.graph import list_edges

    assert list_edges(edited.id) == [{"from_id": edited.id, "to_id": evidence.id, "relation": "derived_from"}]
    assert get_node(requirement.id).status == "stale"
    assert get_node(edited.id).status == "ok"

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import pytest

from app import tools
from app.db import get_conn, init_db
from app.graph import add_node, get_node
from app.models import NodeType, Relation


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clean_db():
    init_db()
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute("TRUNCATE edges, nodes CASCADE")
            cur.execute("UPDATE node_counters SET next = 1")
    yield


def test_source_needs_no_inputs():
    node = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "G70 feedback.xlsx"}, [], "tool:import")
    assert node.id == "SRC-001"
    assert node.status == "ok"


def test_import_source_tool_creates_source():
    node = tools.import_source({"file": "G70 feedback.xlsx"}, "tool:ingestion")
    assert node.type == NodeType.SOURCE


def test_claim_requires_inputs():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        add_node(NodeType.CLAIM, {"text": "unmet need"}, [], "agent:researcher")


def test_decision_requires_pm():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    with pytest.raises(PermissionError):
        add_node(NodeType.DECISION, {"verdict": "approve"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")

    decided = add_node(NodeType.DECISION, {"verdict": "approve"}, [src.id], "PM:alex", relation=Relation.DECIDES)
    assert decided.created_by == "PM:alex"


def test_nodes_are_append_only():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    with get_conn() as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            with pytest.raises(Exception):
                cur.execute("UPDATE nodes SET content = '{}' WHERE id = %s", (src.id,))
                conn.commit()


def test_stale_propagates_to_dependents():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    evidence = tools.query_data({"row": "complaint"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    claim = tools.add_claim({"text": "unmet need"}, [evidence.id], "agent:researcher")

    add_node(
        NodeType.EVIDENCE,
        {"row": "corrected complaint"},
        [src.id],
        "agent:researcher",
        replaces=evidence.id,
    )

    assert get_node(evidence.id).status == "stale"
    assert get_node(claim.id).status == "stale"


def test_add_claim_rejects_missing_input():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        tools.add_claim({"text": "x"}, ["EVD-999"], "agent:researcher")


def test_web_search_creates_evidence_with_url():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    found = tools.web_search({"url": "https://example.com", "quote": "trend"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    assert found.type == NodeType.EVIDENCE
    assert found.content["url"] == "https://example.com"


def test_add_assumption_requires_inputs():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        tools.add_assumption({"text": "guess"}, [], "agent:researcher")


def test_propose_requirement_links_to_claim():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    evidence = tools.query_data({"row": "complaint"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    claim = tools.add_claim({"text": "unmet need"}, [evidence.id], "agent:researcher")
    requirement = tools.propose_requirement({"text": "fix it"}, [claim.id], "agent:researcher")
    assert requirement.type == NodeType.REQUIREMENT


def test_challenge_creates_contradicting_evidence():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    claim = add_node(NodeType.CLAIM, {"text": "unmet need"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    counter = tools.challenge({"row": "actually fine"}, claim.id, "agent:researcher")
    assert counter.type == NodeType.EVIDENCE
    from app.graph import get_dependents
    assert any(d.id == counter.id for d in get_dependents(claim.id))


def test_ask_pm_allows_no_inputs():
    question = tools.ask_pm({"text": "which market first?"}, None, "agent:researcher")
    assert question.type == NodeType.QUESTION


def test_double_versioning_marks_both_old_versions_stale():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    v1 = tools.query_data({"row": "v1"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    v2 = add_node(NodeType.EVIDENCE, {"row": "v2"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher", replaces=v1.id)
    v3 = add_node(NodeType.EVIDENCE, {"row": "v3"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher", replaces=v2.id)

    assert v2.version == 2
    assert v3.version == 3
    assert get_node(v1.id).status == "stale"
    assert get_node(v2.id).status == "stale"
    assert get_node(v3.id).status == "ok"


def test_scoring_a_stale_node_is_still_allowed():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")
    evidence = tools.query_data({"row": "v1"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    claim = tools.add_claim({"text": "unmet need"}, [evidence.id], "agent:researcher")
    requirement = tools.propose_requirement({"text": "fix it"}, [claim.id], "agent:researcher")

    add_node(NodeType.EVIDENCE, {"row": "v2"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher", replaces=evidence.id)
    assert get_node(requirement.id).status == "stale"

    scored = tools.score({"value": 1}, requirement.id, "formula", "formula:v1")
    assert scored.type == NodeType.SCORE
    assert scored.status == "ok"


def test_concurrent_add_node_gets_unique_ids():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "x.csv"}, [], "tool:import")

    def make_claim(i):
        return tools.add_claim({"text": f"claim {i}"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher").id

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) as pool:
        ids = list(pool.map(make_claim, range(8)))

    assert len(set(ids)) == 8


def test_end_to_end_requirement_traces_to_source():
    src = add_node(NodeType.SOURCE, {"file": "G70 feedback.xlsx"}, [], "tool:import")
    evidence = tools.query_data({"row": "seat too narrow"}, [src.id], "agent:researcher")
    claim = tools.add_claim({"text": "seats too narrow for tall drivers"}, [evidence.id], "agent:researcher")
    requirement = tools.propose_requirement({"text": "widen seat by 2cm"}, [claim.id], "agent:researcher")

    scored = tools.score({"value": 7.5, "breakdown": {}}, requirement.id, "impact*reach", "formula:scoring_v1")
    decision = tools.decide({"verdict": "approve"}, requirement.id, "PM:alex", rationale="matches strategy")

    from app.graph import get_inputs

    assert get_inputs(requirement.id)[0].id == claim.id
    assert get_inputs(claim.id)[0].id == evidence.id
    assert get_inputs(evidence.id)[0].id == src.id
    assert scored.type == NodeType.SCORE
    assert decision.created_by.startswith("PM:")
